newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Guinea-Bissau drops peso for CFA franc at midnight.
newsitem.headline: Guinea-Bissau drops peso for CFA franc at midnight.

text.p: The tiny West African state of Guinea-Bissau will become a fully-fledged member of the Franc Zone at midnight on Thursday when it finally abandons its currency, the peso, for the CFA franc.

The two currencies have been circulating in tandem since May when Guinea-Bissau joined the seven other states in the West African Monetary Union (UMOA). They all use the CFA franc, which is linked to the French franc.
A Guinea-Bissau banking official reached by telephone from Dakar said that by July 30 it was estimated that 90 percent of the pesos in circulation had been exchanged for CFA francs.
"As always, some people will wait for the last day to change their pesos into CFA. I am confident everything will go smoothly," he added.
The central bank of UMOA, the BCEAO which is overseeing the changeover, is based in Dakar, the capital of Senegal.
